reasoning: The underlying problem — how linear activation probes for a safety-relevant behavior degrade as labeled data shrinks, and where the reliability "knee" sits — is already directly studied. FAR.AI's "Training Reliable Activation Probes With a Handful of Positive Examples" and the related rare-misalignment-monitoring work explicitly characterize probe accuracy/AUC in the "few vs. thousands" labeled-example regime for honesty/spam detection, finding larger models are more sample-efficient and quantifying positive-sample efficiency. Independent linear-probe label-efficiency results report a near-logarithmic accuracy-vs-label-count relationship with a plateau after ~30-50 labeled responses (the exact "knee" the proposal seeks), and safety-probe work notes effectiveness "with as few as 50 training samples." Sycophancy-specific linear probes as runtime monitors are also already established (arXiv 2412.00967, 2601.16644, 2601.18939, 2511.06419 MONICA). The only un-covered slivers are applying the label-efficiency-curve framing to the sycophancy behavior specifically and a small zero-shot transfer table — incremental gaps, not an open problem, so this is largely addressed rather than partially.

evidence.title: Training Reliable Activation Probes With a Handful of Positive Examples
evidence.summary: Directly studies activation probes for safety-relevant detection (honesty, spam) in the few-vs-thousands labeled-example regime; finds many-negative training is more positive-sample-efficient at 1-10 positives, larger models probe more sample-efficiently, and identifies diminishing-returns patterns — i.e., the label-efficiency question the proposal poses, already answered for analogous behaviors.

evidence.title: Detecting High-Stakes Interactions with Activation Probes (2506.10805)
evidence.summary: Safety-monitoring linear probes shown to be data-efficient, effective with as few as 50 training samples — establishing low-label viability of activation probes as runtime safety monitors.

evidence.title: Beyond Linear Probes: Dynamic Safety Monitoring for Language Models (2509.26238)
evidence.summary: Treats linear probes as the standard data-efficient safety-monitoring baseline, noting they excel with ~100 and work with ~50 training samples, framing label efficiency as a known property.

evidence.title: Linear Probe Accuracy Scales with Model Size and Benefits from Multi-Layer Ensembling (2604.13386)
evidence.summary: Reports the characteristic accuracy-vs-label-count curve: substantial gains and variance reduction within the first 30-50 labeled responses then a plateau, with a near-logarithmic relationship — essentially the 'knee' the proposal aims to locate.

evidence.title: Sycophancy Hides Linearly in the Attention Heads (2601.16644)
evidence.summary: Demonstrates linear sycophancy probes on mid-layer activations achieving high held-out accuracy (e.g., 88.4% on 4B) and AUC-based evaluation, establishing the sycophancy-probe monitor the proposal builds on.

evidence.title: MONICA: Real-Time Monitoring and Calibration of Chain-of-Thought Sycophancy (2511.06419)
evidence.summary: Frames sycophancy detection as supervised logistic-regression probing over activation space for runtime monitoring, the same probe-as-monitor setup the proposal uses.
